steps: Locate the stove
Keep 4" to side and back walls, 18" to the ceiling and 1" to the vent. No floor protector is needed on a floor that is stable and strong enough to support the stove.

Corner placements: the minimum clearances are shown as diagrams (Figures 22 and 23).

  • Freestanding installation only.
  • Do not connect to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning stove.
  • Install and vent per CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or ANSI Z223.1 (USA) and local codes. In Massachusetts, only a licensed plumber and gas fitter may install it.
  • Manufactured (mobile) homes: an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured (mobile) home, where local codes allow (in some jurisdictions, after the "first sale"). Fasten the stove in place; CAN/CSA Z240 MH (Canada), or Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 or ANSI/NFPA 501A (USA).
Maker's website: Standard Features: mobile home approved. Install to the manual.
Vent terminal clearances
The terminal must not be recessed. Measure to the nearest edge of the termination hood and hold the Figure 25 minimums and the roof pitch table.

Measure to the nearest edge of the termination hood. The terminal must not be recessed. Local codes or regulations may require different clearances.

Clearances to adjacent structures are shown only on the Figure 24 drawing.

Massachusetts: a sidewall termination less than 7 feet above grade needs hard-wired CO detection and a "GAS VENT DIRECTLY BELOW. KEEP CLEAR OF ALL OBSTRUCTIONS" sign at least 8 feet above grade (248 CMR 5.08, p. 3).
Co-axial vent layout

Certified 4" x 6-5/8" co-axial only: 30 ft total inside the chart, max three 90° elbows, 2 ft less horizontal run for each 90° after the first. A horizontal termination no higher than 2 ft vertically needs the Snorkel terminal.

• Certified 4" x 6-5/8" co-axial venting components only; approved brands are in the cross-reference charts (p. 21). Mixing manufacturers is inadvisable.
  • Total vent length no more than 30 feet; any rise/run combination inside the chart boundaries. The chart itself is a diagram (Figure 26).
  • Maximum three 90° elbows. One 90° (or equal combination) is allowed without reducing horizontal run; reduce horizontal run by 2 feet for each additional 90°.
  • Support the vent pipe properly.

Snorkel terminal

  • Must be used for a horizontal termination at the end of venting no higher than 2 feet vertically; otherwise the regular terminal can be used.
  • Orient it with the vent inlet and outlet, and the drain ports, at the bottom. Otherwise the exhaust is restricted.
  • Fasten to the exterior wall with the 4 supplied screws. Siding can butt the sides and extend up to 1" from the wall.
  • Caulk where the unit meets the wall and where the siding meets the unit.

Snorkel dimensions are given only as a drawing (Figure 28, p. 19). Sales code 11270002.

The damper ships closed and may need slight adjustment for your vent configuration (last step).
Co-linear chimney option
Through an existing chimney: 3" exhaust and 3" intake flex liners, 10' min to 35' max to termination, with a recommended Duravent co-linear kit.

Recommended: Simpson Duravent High-Wind Co-Linear Kit w/Flex (46DVA-CL33) or Simpson Duravent Prairie Co-Linear Kit w/Flex (46DVA-CL33P).

  1. Measure chimney height and cut the flex liner (min. 10' to termination). Mark one pipe at both ends as the combustion air intake.
  2. Attach the marked pipe to the intake side of the vent terminal and the other to the outlet side; seal and secure with the sealant and screws provided.
  3. Insert both liners from the top of the chimney down through the damper opening.
  4. Apply a bead of caulking to the top of the clay liner, slip the terminal over and secure it with the lateral retaining bolts.
  5. Larger chimneys: construct flashing to local building codes.

Venting through an existing fireplace opening with the co-axial to co-linear adapter (80000268): seal the opening with a cover that leaves the adapter flush, or place the TN24 and adapter outside the opening.
Gas & electrical connection

Position the stove and run the supply line (connector not included) to the 3/8" flare fitting at the rear, with a drip leg and an upstream union. Don't plug in the cord or turn on the gas until installation is complete.

• Gas line by a qualified service person to all building codes; use the correct line diameter for proper operation and pressure.
  • Drip leg in the supply line to the gas control valve, to keep loose scale and dirt out of the valve.
  • Union or flanged connection (not provided) just upstream of the valve.
  • Turn on the gas and check that all connections are tight and leak free.
  • Supply-piping pressure tests above ½ psig (3.5 kPa): disconnect the stove and its shut-off valve. At ½ psig (3.5 kPa) or less: close its shut-off valve.
Note: p. 23 says the gas supply line connects to a 3/8" NPT flare fitting at the rear of the stove; p. 34 says the gas connection accepts a 3/8" 45° flare fitting.

Electrical: an IEC power cord is provided for a standard wall outlet. Blower rating 115 V, 60 Hz, 1.1 A.
Unpack the firebox

Ceramic panels and burner come installed; logs and embers ship in styrofoam behind the glass door and screen. Remove the top cover and screen mesh, then the wing bolts and the glass door with its retainer frame.

1. Remove the top cover.
  2. Raise the screen mesh cover and lift the screen mesh out.
  3. Remove the wing bolts holding the glass door retainer frame, tilt the door and remove it together with its retainer frame.

The large number one log is wrapped separately from the smaller logs. Logs, embers, glass door and screen go back in a specific order.
Embers & log set
Fill the burner basket with embers to overflow the front row, then set logs 1 to 5 in order without covering the burner's back row. No embers between the back row and logs 3 and 4.

1. Fill the burner basket with embers so it overflows the burner front row. Reserve a small amount.
  2. Log 1 on the firebox ledge, set completely against the rear wall.
  3. Log 2: the hole in its back goes over the post on the left of log 1; rest its lower end on the tab beside the pilot, close to the front but clear of the glass door.
  4. Log 3: the hole in its underside fits the burner's protruding tab; don't cover the back-row burner holes.
  5. Log 4: black charcoal side facing inward; it supports the final log.
  6. Log 5: don't cover the back-row burner holes.
  7. Fill leftover spaces with the reserved embers.
Don't place embers between the burner's back row and the back of logs 3 and 4: it interferes with airflow and gives a sooty flame.

Exact log positions are shown in photos (Figures 45 to 52, pp. 26 to 28).
Glass door & screen
Seat the door frame in the firebox floor slot, align its stud and tighten the wing bolts without over-tightening. Fit the screen mesh rear side toward the logs, then refit the top cover.

1. Lower the glass door frame so it fits the horizontal slot on the firebox floor.
  2. Align it laterally so the protruding positioning stud fits the firebox slot; this lines up the bolt holes.
  3. Insert and tighten the wing bolts. Over-tightening could fracture the glass door.
  4. Screen mesh: rear side toward the log set, front side out. The frame is not square, so check its orientation first.
  5. Seat the bottom edge firmly in the firebox frame channel; lower the top holder so its channels secure the top (a small amount of force may be needed).
  6. Return the top cover.

The screen protects from heat radiating from the glass door. Use only the glass and screen barrier certified with the appliance.
Initialize IFC & remote

4 AA in the rear battery bay with the selection switch on Remote, 3 AAA in the handset; plug in and open the gas. Press PRG with a paper clip (3 beeps), then the remote's power button (4 beeps = synchronized).

1. 4 AA batteries in the battery bay at the rear; selection switch on "Remote".
  2. 3 AAA batteries in the Proflame 2 remote.
  3. Plug the power cord into a wall socket and open the gas supply line.
  4. With a straightened paper clip, press the program button once through the "PRG" opening in the ON/OFF battery bay cover. The IFC beeps 3 times: ready to synchronize.
  5. Press the remote's power button once. 4 beeps: remote and control module are synchronized.

Pilot mode: with the system off, Mode to the CPI icon, then Up for CPI or Down for IPI (p. 10). A double-beep from the IFC on a command means its batteries are low (p. 11).
Damper, venturi & pressure
Damper ships closed: open slowly to clear a sagging, sooting flame. Venturi closed for natural gas, open for propane. Check inlet and manifold pressure with the stove lit at its highest setting.

Damper

Under the top cladding cover plate. Factory setting is closed; slowly open and adjust as necessary to eliminate a sagging, sooting flame.

Venturi

Through the opening in the rear cover. Loosen the wing nut, move the post up to open or down to close, then tighten. Closed for natural gas, open for liquid propane.

Gas pressure test (p. 35)

  1. Turn off the gas supply before loosening the test point screws.
  2. Remove the rear panel and locate the valve and its inlet and manifold pressure test points; loosen the screws with a flat-tip screwdriver.
  3. Attach the gauge, turn the gas back on and test with the stove lit and at the highest setting.
  4. Turn off the gas, remove the gauges and re-tighten the test point screws.

Pilot flame: adjust with the pilot adjustment screw on the valve.

panels.title: Sagging or sooty flame
items: Damper still at its factory-closed setting → open slowly until the flame clears
Embers between the burner's back row and logs 3 and 4 → blocked airflow, sooty flame
Heavy soot on logs or burner at inspection → qualified service person to adjust combustion

panels.title: Low battery
items: Low-battery icon on the remote screen → replace the remote's 3 AAA batteries
IFC double-beeps when it receives a command → IFC batteries (4 AA) low
Remote or receiver batteries depleted → turn off at the ON/OFF switch on the rear battery holder

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
There's no knob to turn or match to strike. The stove's control module lights it automatically when you switch it on with the remote.

  1. Check that the selection switch on the battery bay at the back of the stove is set to Remote, so the handset can be used.
  2. With the stove off, press the ON/OFF key on the remote. The stove's receiver gives a single beep to confirm.
  3. Wait. The pilot may take up to 30 seconds to ignite each time you turn the stove on. That's normal.

Turning it off

With the stove on, press ON/OFF again. The remote's screen goes back to showing only the room temperature, and the receiver beeps once.

Keep away from the burner while you use the remote. The receiver is what lights the stove, and it can come on suddenly.

The manual prints its full lighting instructions only as a diagram (Figure 20) on page 13, so check that page too.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs on 3 AAA batteries. Its keys are ON/OFF, Thermostat, the Up/Down arrows and Mode. The stove confirms each command with a single beep.

Flame height

There are six flame levels. Press Down to lower the flame one step at a time, all the way to off. Press Up to raise it. If the stove is on but the flame is off, pressing Up brings the flame back on high.

Thermostat

  • Room thermostat: press the Thermostat key. The screen shows the thermostat is on, with the set temperature. Use Up/Down to change it.
  • Smart thermostat: press Thermostat until "SMART" appears. The flame turns down as the room gets close to your set point, and up when the room is cool.

Key lock and F / C

Press Mode and Up together to lock the keys (a lock icon appears). Do it again to unlock. With the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode together, then check the screen shows F or C beside the room temperature.

sounds.title: First fire: smells and sounds
sounds.html:
A slight odor the first time

When you light the stove for the first time, it gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours. That's the paints, sealants, gaskets and lubricants from manufacturing curing in the heat. It's temporary.

  • Open doors and windows to air out the room.
  • Some people find the curing smell uncomfortable.

Ticks and pings

Steel stoves make some expansion and contraction noises as they start up and cool down. It's the same kind of sound your furnace or oven makes, and it's normal.

A short wait before the flame

The pilot may take up to 30 seconds to ignite each time you turn the stove on.

A gas smell is different. If you smell gas, don't try to light anything and don't touch switches or phones in the building. Leave, and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it, using fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Wait until it's cool. Never clean the glass while it's hot.
  • No abrasive cleaners, on the glass or on any other part of the stove.
  • The outside finish can be cleaned with mild soap and water.
  • Don't strike or knock the glass in any way that could break it.
Cracked or broken glass? Don't use the stove until the glass door is replaced. Get the replacement from your True North dealer (don't substitute any other type), and have a licensed or qualified service person fit it.

At the yearly inspection, the glass gasket is checked and replaced if needed. The glass seal has to stay in good condition.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
The stove's control module can run the pilot two ways, and you choose with the remote:

IPIintermittent pilot ignition
CPIcontinuous pilot ignition

To switch modes

  1. Turn the stove off with the remote.
  2. Press Mode until the CPI icon shows.
  3. Press Up to turn on continuous pilot (CPI), or Down to go back to intermittent pilot (IPI).
  4. A single beep confirms the change.

In either mode, the control module lights the pilot automatically and watches the pilot flame. It runs on house power, with batteries as backup.

fan.title: Blowers and accent light
fan.html:
Your stove has a right and a left blower fan, plus an accent light under the stove. You run both from the remote.

Fan speed

Press Mode until the fan icon shows, then use Up/Down to turn the fan on or off, or pick one of six speeds. A single beep confirms.

Accent light

Press Mode until the light bulb icon shows, then use Up/Down to set one of six brightness levels.

Changing the colored glass

The stove comes with glass plates in various colors. The plate sits in a holder under the light tray, underneath the stove, and slides in from the front.

Let the glass plate cool before you change it.

power.title: Power and batteries
power.html:
The stove plugs into a standard wall outlet. Its control module runs on that house power, with a battery pack as backup, so you can still use the stove during a power outage.

Battery bay, back of stove4 AA
Remote3 AAA

Low-battery signals

  • Remote: a low-battery icon appears on the screen before the power runs out. It goes away when you put in new batteries.
  • Stove: if the control module double-beeps when it gets a command, its batteries are low. With new batteries it goes back to a single beep.
Batteries dead? You can still turn the stove off with the ON/OFF switch on the battery holder at the back of the stove. Keep clear of the burner when you use it.

Pairing the remote

The first-time setup pairs them: with batteries in both, press the program button through the "PRG" opening in the battery bay cover with a straightened paper clip (the stove beeps 3 times), then press the remote's power button once (it beeps 4 times).

gassmell.title: If you smell gas
gassmell.html:
The manual's cover lists what to do if you ever smell gas:

  1. Don't try to light any appliance.
  2. Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  3. Leave the building right away.
  4. From a neighbor's phone, call your gas supplier right away and follow their instructions.
  5. If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.
Keep flammables away. Don't store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids near this or any other appliance.

Only a qualified installer, service agency or the gas supplier should install or service the stove. Don't try to repair it yourself; if you find a problem, call your dealer.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• Hot glass burns. Don't touch the glass until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. The barrier that comes with the stove must be installed to protect children and others at risk.
  • The stove runs at high temperatures. Keep it out of traffic and away from furniture and drapes. Don't put clothing or anything flammable on or near it.
  • Watch young children closely when they're in the room. If anyone at risk lives with you, a physical barrier is recommended; an adjustable safety gate can keep them out of the room.
  • Any grill, panel or door removed for service must go back on before you use the stove.
  • Don't run the stove with the glass door removed, cracked or broken.
Been under water? If any part of the stove has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the stove and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Annual service and care
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the stove and its venting at least once a year. The manual says it should be inspected by a professional before use and at least annually. Lint from carpets or bedding can mean cleaning more often.

What the yearly check covers

  • Logs, embers and burner checked for soot; burners cleaned with a brush or vacuum, especially the burner ports.
  • Pilot checked for proper flame size and cleaned.
  • Vent pipe and outside vent terminal checked for blockage or debris.
  • Glass gasket checked, and replaced if needed.
  • Batteries checked and replaced as needed.

Heavy soot means a service person needs to adjust the stove for proper combustion. The control compartments, burners and air passages must be kept clean.

Before any servicing, turn off the gas and electrical supply and give the stove plenty of time to cool. Keep the area around it clear of anything combustible, and don't try to repair it yourself: call your dealer.

specElec.html:

Don't plug in the cord until installation is complete. The Proflame 2 IFC runs on AC with the battery pack as DC backup during an AC power interruption; it also controls the comfort fan (off plus six speeds) and the dimmable accent light.

The receiver is powered by line voltage: don't open its enclosure, and disconnect line voltage before maintenance. Label all wires before disconnecting when servicing controls; the wiring diagram (p. 38) is a drawing.

specConv.title: Propane conversion
specConv.html:
KitTN24.LPKITA · sales code 32180001
Contentspilot and burner orifices, pressure modulator
Burner orifice½" socket · Loctite 567 Thread Sealant
Pilot orifice5/32" or 4mm Allen · 9 lbf in (1 Nm)
  1. Shut off the gas supply and let the stove cool to room temperature.
  2. Switch the valve's pressure modulator per the instructions with the kit.
  3. Remove the mesh and glass doors, log set, embers and burner. The burner orifice is at the lower inside rear of the firebox.
  4. Pilot: remove the spring, pull the hood up off the pilot bracket and turn the orifice counter-clockwise to remove it. Fit the new one, then refit the hood (tab to the slot in the pilot journal) and the spring.
  5. Adjust the venturi shutter: open for propane (p. 33).

review.notes: Lighting instructions (p. 13) exist only as a diagram (Figure 20) with no readable text; not transcribed. The light drawer describes the remote start from pp. 6, 8, 11 and 32 and links p. 13. Also left as diagrams, not transcribed: corner-placement clearances (Figs. 22-23, p. 15), adjacent-structure dimensions in Fig. 24 (p. 16), the co-axial venting envelope (Fig. 26, p. 17), Snorkel dimensions (Fig. 28, p. 19), the unlabeled dimension in Fig. 21 (p. 14), log positions (photos, pp. 26-28) and the wiring diagram (p. 38). No warranty terms in the manual (p. 4 only says deviations void the Pacific Energy Fireplaces Warranty), so no warranty tile. No troubleshooting chart or code table: fault panels use the manual's own fault descriptions (sooting flame pp. 12, 28, 33; low-battery signals pp. 8, 11); codes left empty and beep signals described in drawers. p. 34 lists AFUE 73.0% while the rating label gives P.4.1-15 efficiency 74.4%: different metrics, not flagged as a conflict; the catalog's P.4.1 figure matches the label. Catalog items the manual doesn't cover: blower cfm, glass area, leveling legs. The remote section's fan text is conditional ('if the gas stove is equipped with a hot air circulating fan'), while pp. 22, 37 and 39 show right and left blowers on this model. The pressure-test text says 'inlet and outlet test points'; Fig. 73 labels them inlet and manifold pressure test points. One stray glyph on p. 1 decoded with the 29-code-point rule ('buildingK' = 'building.'). Footers on pp. 2-3 carry an older revision code (150118-40).
